datasets: Violent Crime Rate per 1,000 Residents by CSA (BNIA Vital Signs; synthetic stand-in)
Neighborhood Businesses per 1,000 Residents by CSA (BNIA Vital Signs; synthetic stand-in)
build_error: go build ./... fails (no go.mod): 'directory prefix . does not contain main module'; documented 'go build -o baltimore main.go' succeeds
concurrency_primitives: 2 goroutines + sync.WaitGroup per dataset (main.go:224-229); per-CSV bounded worker pool: jobs/parsed channels cap 4*workers, N parser goroutines, reader goroutine, single collector owning map (main.go:62-110)
design_patterns: Implicit pipeline (loadCSV -> join -> score -> display/JSON); single file, no named pattern
questions: Which CSAs have the highest violent crime rate?
Which CSAs have the lowest business density?
How strongly are the two rates associated (Pearson correlation)?
Which CSAs score highest on an exploratory crime-plus-low-business priority index?
Which CSAs have the largest numerical difference between the two rates?
overview: Single-file Go program with clean functional decomposition (loadCSV worker pool, join, correlation, score, display, JSON writer) and flag-driven column mapping. The parsing stage uses a correct bounded worker pool with channels and a single collector; join and scoring are sequential. No go.mod, no tests, no packages.
stakeholder_value: No stakeholder is named, and all five answers (Pearson r=0.834, priority index, rate gaps) are computed from ten admittedly invented values per file, so nothing can be learned about Baltimore. The priority-index idea (Q4) would be useful on real Vital Signs exports; Q5 subtracts incommensurable rates.
issues: Both CSVs are synthetic 10-row files (README admits); no fetch script or generator; real data absent
No go.mod: go build ./..., go vet ./..., go test ./... all fail
Worker pool only in parsing; join/aggregate sequential
No tests, no named stakeholder, Q1/Q2 single-dataset
rationale: Builds and runs cleanly with a real worker pool and documented memory design, earning solid build/concurrency/memory credit. Near-zero real_data because the inputs are fabricated with no way to obtain real data, which also halves stakeholder and runs_results credit since every answer is meaningless. Single-file, untested layout without go.mod limits architecture. 52/100 = F.
